items.title: Build the money-path verification harness: property, mutation, idempotency and independent model
items.outcome: Every money-path module is verified by generated properties, by a second independent implementation, by a mutation threshold and by an adversarial retry suite, and each of those is a gate rather than a habit.
items.context: The test strategy names independent-model verification and mutation testing as principles, but nothing enforces them. For financial arithmetic, tests written by the same author against the same misunderstanding pass happily. This harness is what makes a wrong number a build failure.
scope: Shared property-based generators for amounts, currencies, dates, schedules and split shares
Invariant suite covering zero-sum, non-negative-where-required, rounding and period-boundary rules
Independent second implementation of debt, budgeting and allocation arithmetic used as an oracle
Mutation testing configured with a threshold that fails the build on money-path packages
Idempotency and adversarial retry suite covering duplicate, concurrent and out-of-order writes
Threshold wiring that reads the per-package numeric floors from docs#21 rather than restating them in the harness
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately introduced rounding error in a money-path module is caught by the property suite
A disagreement between the implementation and the independent model fails the build and names the case

Mutation score below the numeric floor published by docs#21 for that named package fails the build on money-path packages only; the harness reads the published number and never an agreed threshold nobody wrote down
A duplicated financial write with the same idempotency key produces exactly one ledger effect
Concurrent writes to the same account under a serializable transaction never produce a negative or unbalanced state
The harness runs within the numeric pipeline budget published by docs#21, so it is not disabled for speed, and exceeding that budget fails rather than warns
Line and branch coverage on every money-path package meets the numeric floor published by docs#21 for that package, and a package with no published number fails the run rather than defaulting
contracts_schema: Consumes the money representation and idempotency conventions and fails if an endpoint accepts a financial write without a key
security_privacy: Generators produce synthetic data only; no production-derived values are used
Failure output must not print full records, only the minimal reproducing case
observability: Publishes mutation score, property case count and oracle disagreement count per run
tests: Independent-model comparison across the full case matrix
rollout_rollback: Introduced as non-blocking for one week to establish the baseline, then made blocking
Rollback is lowering the mutation threshold with a recorded expiry, never removing the gate
non_goals: Feature-level tests, which each feature ticket owns
Load and performance testing, which is a separate ticket

items.title: Run provider and consumer contract testing against the published specification
items.outcome: A breaking contract change fails the provider pull request, and a consumer that drifts from the published contract fails its own pipeline, so cross-repository work can proceed in parallel safely.
items.context: Contract-first sequencing is the stated protocol for cross-repository change, but nothing verifies it. Without provider and consumer verification the contract becomes documentation and the generated clients diverge quietly.
scope: Provider verification that the running service satisfies the published specification
Consumer verification for the generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients
Compatibility checking that classifies a change as additive or breaking
Pipeline wiring so both directions run on the relevant pull requests
Published report identifying which consumer versions are compatible with which contract version
acceptance_criteria: Removing a response field fails the provider pull request unless the expand and contract protocol was followed
A consumer using a field the contract no longer offers fails its own pipeline
Additive changes pass without consumer changes
The compatibility report names each consumer and its verified contract version
Verification runs against the published artifact, not a branch build
The Python consumer is verified on the same terms as the Kotlin and TypeScript consumers; a Python client that drifts from the published contract fails its own pipeline
The compatibility report names the Python consumer explicitly, so a missing Python row is a failure rather than an omission
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 document is the contract of record; verification consumes the published artifact
security_privacy: Verification fixtures contain synthetic data only
No production endpoint is called during verification
observability: Publishes contract version, consumer versions verified and the compatibility verdict
tests: Python consumer verification against the published artifact
rollout_rollback: Enabled for additive detection first, then breaking-change blocking once the baseline is clean
Rollback is downgrading the gate to warning with a recorded expiry
non_goals: Writing endpoint specifications, which the contract expansion tickets own

items.title: Build the tenancy, object-authorization and authentication attack suite
items.outcome: An automated suite actively attempts cross-tenant reads, broken object authorization, mass assignment and authentication bypass, from both inside the code and from outside the running service, and any success fails the pipeline.
items.context: Isolation is asserted by design documents but never attacked. Assertions that a query filters by tenant prove intent; attempts that try to read another tenant's rows prove behaviour. The audit calls out that only tests which actually try are acceptable here.
scope: White-box tests exercising database policies directly with a foreign tenant context
Black-box tests against the running service using enumerated and guessed identifiers
Object-level authorization coverage report across the endpoint inventory
Mass assignment and parameter tampering attempts on every write endpoint
Authentication bypass attempts including expired, revoked, replayed and forged credentials
acceptance_criteria: Every attempt to read or write another tenant's record is denied and recorded
An endpoint added without an object-level authorization check fails the coverage report and the build
Sending an unexpected privileged field in a write payload does not change it
A replayed or revoked token is rejected and the attempt is auditable
Under pooled connections and concurrent load, no request observes another tenant's session context
A deliberately weakened policy in a test fixture causes the suite to fail, proving the suite works
contracts_schema: Consumes the endpoint inventory from the published specification so new endpoints are detected automatically
security_privacy: Suite runs against synthetic tenants only
Findings are reported without printing the leaked record contents
observability: Publishes attempted, denied and unexpectedly allowed counts per run and alerts on any allowed
rollout_rollback: Runs in the pull request pipeline for the fast subset and nightly for the full suite
A failing suite blocks deploy; there is no waiver path in the pipeline
non_goals: Penetration testing by an external party, which is a separate ticket
Implementing the isolation controls themselves, which belongs to E19

items.title: Enforce static analysis, dynamic scanning, dependency and secret gates with flaky-test quarantine
items.outcome: Static application security testing, dynamic scanning of a running build, dependency review and secret scanning all run as blocking gates, and flaky tests are quarantined automatically instead of being retried into green.
items.context: Secret scanning and dependency review are already required but static and dynamic security testing have no owner, and there is no flaky-test policy implementation. Silent retries are how a real failure becomes invisible.
scope: Static application security testing per language with an agreed rule set and severity gate
Dynamic scanning against an ephemeral deployed build for the authenticated and unauthenticated surface
Dependency review with a severity threshold and an exception process with expiry
Full-history secret scanning and a rotation trigger on detection
Automatic quarantine after a defined number of flakes, which opens a ticket rather than muting silently
acceptance_criteria: A planted injection-prone pattern is caught by static analysis and fails the pull request
A dynamic scan of the running build reports and fails on a high severity finding
A dependency with a high severity advisory fails the build unless an exception with an expiry exists
A planted secret is blocked and triggers a rotation ticket automatically
A test that flakes beyond the threshold is quarantined and a ticket is created; a quarantined test cannot silently disappear
No pipeline step retries a failing test more than the policy allows
contracts_schema: Scan results published in a machine-readable format consumed by the release checklist
security_privacy: Scanners run against ephemeral environments with synthetic data only
Scanner credentials are short lived and scoped to the ephemeral environment
observability: Publishes finding counts by severity, exception count with expiry dates and quarantine population
rollout_rollback: Introduced as warning-only for one week to measure noise, then made blocking
Rollback is returning a specific rule to warning with a recorded expiry
non_goals: Penetration testing, which is a separate ticket
Fixing findings, which is owned by the repository where the finding lives

items.title: Build load, stress, soak and chaos suites and run a disaster-recovery game day
items.outcome: The system is exercised at peak load, past peak, for a sustained period and under deliberate component failure, and a disaster-recovery game day proves the restore path works under time pressure.
items.context: None of load, stress, soak, chaos or a recovery game day has an owner. For a financial application the failure modes that matter, such as a key service outage or a connection pool exhaustion, are exactly the ones that never appear in functional tests.
scope: Load profiles for realistic peak traffic with latency and error budgets
Stress profile that finds the breaking point and records the failure mode
Sustained soak run checking for memory growth, connection leaks and counter drift
Fault injection covering database failover, key service outage, cache loss, provider outage and webhook storms
Disaster-recovery game day restoring into a clean environment against the clock
acceptance_criteria: Peak load meets the published latency and error budgets and a regression fails the release
The stress run records the breaking point and the system degrades rather than corrupting data
A sustained run shows no unbounded memory or connection growth and quota counters remain exact
Each injected fault has a defined, observed behaviour; a key service outage must never corrupt or expose data
The game day meets the published recovery objectives and the runbook is corrected afterwards
All runs use synthetic data and an isolated environment
contracts_schema: Load profiles and budgets published so a regression can be attributed to a specific endpoint
security_privacy: No production traffic replay and no production data in any profile
Fault injection is confined to non-production environments
observability: Publishes latency percentiles, error rates, saturation and the observed failure mode per run
tests: Soak run with leak and drift assertions
Fault injection scenarios with expected behaviour assertions
rollout_rollback: Run on a schedule and before each release candidate; failures block promotion
Rollback is not applicable; a failed run blocks rather than changes production
non_goals: Application performance optimisation, which belongs to the owning feature ticket
Client-side performance budgets, which are separate tickets

items.title: Gate the web application on end-to-end journeys, accessibility and performance budgets
items.outcome: Critical web journeys are covered by end-to-end tests, accessibility conformance is checked automatically and by a keyboard and screen-reader walkthrough, and performance budgets fail a pull request that regresses them.
items.context: Accessibility is inconsistent across screens and no target level is stated anywhere, and performance budgets exist only as a sentence in the release checklist. On a screen where people read their debt position, an unreadable or unusable page is a product failure.
scope: End-to-end coverage of login, transaction entry, payoff view, import and export
Automated accessibility checks against a named WCAG 2.2 AA ruleset and its pinned version, with zero critical violations on core journeys
Keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthrough evidence for each core journey
Text scaling and zoom verification without truncation or overlap
Performance budgets for load, interactivity and bundle size enforced per pull request
Locale-aware INR formatting checks covering symbol placement, the Indian digit grouping convention and the decimal separator
Pseudo-localization run over every core journey to surface hardcoded strings and truncation before a translator is ever hired
Long-string and right-to-left layout safety checks on every core screen
Latest-stable Chromium, Firefox and WebKit coverage at desktop and representative mobile viewports
Client state coverage check asserting every web surface handles every applicable T-UX-01 state identifier
acceptance_criteria: Each critical journey passes end to end against a seeded synthetic environment
Automated accessibility scanning reports zero critical violations on core journeys
A keyboard-only user can complete every core journey and the evidence is attached
Monetary values carry accessible labels so a screen reader announces them unambiguously
Content remains readable and operable at two hundred percent text scaling
A deliberate bundle size or interactivity regression fails the pull request
Every monetary value renders through the locale-aware INR formatter; a hardcoded currency symbol, grouping or separator fails the check
A pseudo-localized build completes every core journey with no hardcoded string, no clipped label and no concatenated sentence fragment
Core screens survive a long-string locale and a right-to-left layout without overlap, clipping or unmirrored directional affordances
These are MVP quality criteria for the single-currency INR product; multi-currency behaviour is not claimed and remains E30 work
Critical journeys pass independently on latest-stable Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and a browser-specific failure is reported by engine
The conformance target is WCAG 2.2 AA, stated explicitly, and the automated ruleset and its version are named in the configuration rather than left to the tool default
The WCAG 2.2 additions that apply to this product - focus appearance, target size, dragging alternatives and redundant entry - are each covered by a named check or a recorded manual walkthrough step
A rule that the automated scanner cannot decide is routed to the manual walkthrough rather than silently passing
The client state coverage check fails when a surface omits an applicable T-UX-01 state identifier, proven with a planted omission
contracts_schema: Journeys are driven through the published contract; no test reaches into internal state
security_privacy: Tests use synthetic accounts; no production credentials exist in the suite
Recorded artifacts are scrubbed of any test personal data before upload
observability: Publishes journey pass rate, accessibility violation counts and budget headroom per run
tests: Manual keyboard and screen-reader walkthrough with recorded evidence
Performance budget checks with a planted regression test
Locale-aware INR formatting tests including grouping and separator cases
Pseudo-localization journey run with hardcoded-string and truncation detection
Long-string and right-to-left layout safety checks
Per-engine planted regression proving Chromium, Firefox and WebKit matrix failures are isolated and blocking

Quarantine policy applies; a quarantined journey creates a ticket and blocks release if it is a core journey

items.title: Procure and provision the physical Android test device
items.outcome: A dedicated mid-range Android device with an Indian SIM and synthetic test account is physically available, securely provisioned and capable of exercising real SMS and notification permission behavior.
items.context: Device procurement has lead time but no technical prerequisite. Splitting it from corpus governance lets acquisition start immediately while T-QA-12 waits for the published test strategy.

Provision a dedicated synthetic test account with no personal financial data
Record operating-system, OEM, memory and permission capabilities in the device inventory
Verify receipt of structurally realistic bank-format test SMS without retaining a real person's message
Exercise notification restricted-settings, grant and revocation paths
Define and execute secure wipe between test campaigns
acceptance_criteria: The device and SIM are physically available and recorded in the controlled inventory
No personal account, real bank credential or real financial message is stored on the device
A structurally realistic test SMS can be received and exercised by the application test harness

A wipe returns the device to the documented clean state between campaigns
Device capabilities and limitations are recorded for T-QA-12

security_privacy: Only synthetic accounts and messages are used; a real message may be observed to learn structure but is never copied, photographed, attached or retained
The device is access-controlled, encrypted and wiped between campaigns

Notification grant, restricted-settings and revocation smoke tests
Secure-wipe verification against the documented clean-state checklist

items.title: Publish the sanitized parser corpus and Android compatibility matrix
items.outcome: Parser changes run against a privacy-safe corpus and a representative Android compatibility matrix, so format, operating-system, low-memory and OEM-specific regressions fail before release.
items.context: Physical device procurement has no technical dependency and is split into T-QA-07. Corpus governance and the wider compatibility matrix do depend on the test strategy, and they need a separate owner so procurement can start without waiting.
scope: Synthetic, structurally faithful bank-message corpus with an automated privacy scan
Versioned corpus schema and contribution protocol that forbids pasting a real message
Emulator coverage for the oldest supported and current Android releases
Managed-device coverage for low-memory hardware and at least two representative OEM Android variants with aggressive background restrictions
Physical-device runner integration using the provisioned T-QA-07 device
acceptance_criteria: No corpus entry contains a real account number, name, amount or message identifier, proven by an automated scan
A newly observed format is transcribed into synthetic structure under review rather than copied from a real message
Parser and permission journeys pass on the oldest supported release and the current release
Background capture and recovery are exercised on two representative OEM variants and on a low-memory profile
A parser change cannot merge when the corpus or required compatibility subset regresses
Corpus coverage by issuer and rule version is published with no raw content
contracts_schema: Corpus entries carry issuer pattern, rule version, structured synthetic input and expected parse output under a versioned schema
Compatibility-matrix records identify OS, memory class, OEM variant, test subset and result
security_privacy: No real message is committed, attached to an issue, uploaded as a test artifact or printed on failure
Managed devices use synthetic accounts and are wiped after each campaign
observability: Publishes corpus size and coverage plus compatibility pass rate by OS, memory class and OEM variant
tests: Corpus privacy scan with planted identifiers
Parser regression against the complete corpus
Oldest and current Android instrumented matrix
Low-memory and representative OEM background-restriction tests
Physical-device permission and parser smoke test
rollout_rollback: Fast emulator and corpus subsets run on pull requests; the complete managed and physical matrix runs on release candidates
A required matrix failure blocks release; a quarantined case receives an owner and expiry and cannot silently disappear

items.title: Run the per-epic STRIDE threat-model refresh at Definition of Ready
items.outcome: Every epic carries a dated STRIDE threat-model refresh with a named owner before its first ticket starts, the currently missing categories are added, and the refresh has a published cadence rather than being done once and forgotten.
items.context: The existing threat model has no entries for billing forgery, entitlement tampering, AI service compromise, request forgery, prompt injection, split manipulation or administrative single sign-on compromise, and no mechanism refreshes it. It was previously bundled with the external penetration test, which put a Sprint 02 activity behind a pre-launch one. The refresh is cheap, it is the input every security decision reads, and it belongs at Definition of Ready where it can still change a design.
scope: STRIDE refresh template with the per-category prompts and the evidence a refresh must record

The seven currently missing categories added with named owners: billing forgery, entitlement tampering, AI service compromise, request forgery, prompt injection, split manipulation and administrative identity compromise
Definition of Ready item requiring a dated refresh for the epic before its first ticket starts
Published cadence for re-refreshing an epic that is still open, and the trigger events that force an early refresh
Machine-readable refresh record per epic: epic, date, owner, categories reviewed, findings raised
Handoff of each finding to an owning ticket rather than leaving it in the model
acceptance_criteria: Every epic entering implementation has a dated threat-model refresh record naming its owner and the categories reviewed
The model contains all seven previously missing categories, each with an owner
The refresh record is machine-readable, so T-GOV-04 can check it without a human reading the document
The cadence is published as a number of weeks or a named trigger, and an epic whose refresh is older than the cadence is reported as stale
Every finding raised by a refresh is either closed or handed to a named ticket; a finding with no owner fails the refresh
A refresh that reviews fewer than the required categories is invalid rather than partially credited
contracts_schema: Refresh record published as machine-readable data with a documented schema, consumed by the T-GOV-04 check
security_privacy: The threat model names attack paths and controls; it contains no credential, no live endpoint and no customer data
A refresh record is visible to everyone who can see the repository, because a threat model nobody reads is not a control
observability: Count of epics with a current refresh, a stale refresh and no refresh is reported without opening the board
tests: Schema test on the refresh record
Stale-refresh detection test with the clock advanced past the cadence
Invalid-refresh test omitting a required category
rollout_rollback: The template and the seven categories land first, then the Definition of Ready item, then the automated check in T-GOV-04
Rollback removes the automated check; the refresh records already written remain valid evidence
non_goals: The independent penetration test and red-team scenarios, which T-QA-10 owns
Implementing any mitigation, which belongs to the ticket a finding is handed to
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Owns the threat-model template, the category list, the refresh records and the Definition of Ready item. T-GOV-04 owns the pull request check that reads the records.

items.title: Gate the admin console on operator journeys, accessibility and performance
items.outcome: The admin console has the same class of quality gate the customer surfaces have: end-to-end operator journeys, WCAG 2.2 AA conformance, performance budgets, and a planted-defect check proving the redaction, unmask and four-eyes controls actually fail when they are broken.
items.context: The admin console is the highest-privilege surface in the product and the only client with no quality gate. That is exactly backwards: a redaction that silently stops redacting is invisible in code review and catastrophic in production. Accessibility is not optional here either - an operator surface excluded from the accessibility bar is a hiring constraint disguised as a technical decision.
scope: End-to-end operator journeys: search a subject, read redacted data, request an unmask, approve as the second pair of eyes, and complete a support-verified action
Planted-defect gate: deliberately weakened redaction, unmask without an open verified ticket, and a self-approved four-eyes action must all fail the suite
WCAG 2.2 AA conformance with a named, pinned ruleset and a keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthrough
Performance budgets for the console's list and detail surfaces
Client state coverage against the T-UX-01 identifiers, including permission-denied and degraded
Evidence capture so the console's controls can be demonstrated to a reviewer without a live production session
acceptance_criteria: Each operator journey passes end to end against a seeded synthetic environment with no production data
A deliberately weakened redaction rule fails the suite, proving the redaction assertions are meaningful rather than incidental
An unmask attempted with no open verified support ticket fails the suite, and a four-eyes action approved by its own initiator fails the suite
The conformance target is WCAG 2.2 AA, stated explicitly, with the automated ruleset and its version named in the configuration
A keyboard-only operator can complete every journey and the evidence is attached
A deliberate performance regression fails the pull request
The client state coverage check fails when a console surface omits an applicable T-UX-01 state identifier
No test fixture contains real customer data, proven by an automated scan
contracts_schema: Consumes the published administrative contract; the suite asserts contract-level responses rather than internal state
security_privacy: Every fixture is synthetic; the suite never runs against production and holds no production credential
The planted-defect cases are the security value of this ticket: they prove the insider-risk controls fail closed
Evidence artifacts carry no unmasked value, even from synthetic data, so an artifact cannot become a training set for a real one
observability: Suite results are published per journey and per control, so a regression names the control it broke rather than a test file
tests: WCAG 2.2 AA automated scan plus keyboard walkthrough evidence
Fixture scan for real customer data
rollout_rollback: Journeys land as the console surfaces land, with the planted-defect cases added at the same time as the control they test
Rollback disables the gate, which is why the planted-defect cases are recorded as release-blocking rather than advisory
non_goals: Building the console surfaces, which T-ADM-04 and T-ADM-07 to T-ADM-11 own
Server-side administrative controls, which T-ADM-01 to T-ADM-06 own
The malicious-operator red-team suite, which T-ADM-12 owns
Penetration testing, which T-QA-10 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo admin. Owns the operator journey suites, the planted-defect cases and the budget configuration. The controls themselves are implemented in api and rendered by the console shell and its capability screens.

items.title: Run the executable MVP and private-beta evidence gate
items.outcome: One executable gate collects the evidence that private beta may start - contract verification, the data protection floor, the compliance floor, the Android journeys, the traffic capture, a rehearsed rollback and the trust surfaces - and fails with the named missing item rather than producing a checklist somebody signs.
items.context: The plan has a HOLD model, a compliance floor and a release checklist, and no single thing that decides whether beta may start. A checklist a person ticks is not a gate: it passes on a good day and it passes on a bad one. This gate reads the evidence the other tickets already produce - test results, capture artifacts, drill records, published policies - and refuses when one is missing, stale or failing.
scope: Executable gate that reads evidence artifacts from every contributing ticket rather than asking a human
Contract evidence: provider and consumer verification green across all three generated clients
Security evidence: the data protection floor live in the beta environment, with the isolation suite passing and a proven restore
Compliance evidence: consent ledger, purpose registry, rights path, retention jobs, data safety declaration and the breach drill record
Android evidence: instrumented journeys, accessibility and performance budgets, and a staged rollout that can be halted
Privacy evidence: traffic capture proving no raw message content egresses on the release candidate
Rollback evidence: a rehearsed deploy rollback and a rehearsed release halt, both dated
Trust evidence: the user-visible transparency, export, deletion and consent surfaces present and generated from real payloads
Freshness rule: every artifact carries a date and an artifact older than the published window fails the gate
acceptance_criteria: Running the gate produces a pass or a fail and, on failure, names each missing, stale or failing artifact and the ticket that owns it
The gate fails when any single contributing artifact is absent, proven by a test that removes one
The gate fails when an artifact is present but older than the published freshness window, proven with an aged fixture
The gate cannot be passed by a manual override; an exception requires a recorded, dated, expiring waiver with a named owner, and an expired waiver fails
Every contributing ticket is named in the gate definition, so an unowned requirement cannot exist in it
The gate is run and green before any real user account exists in the beta environment
contracts_schema: Evidence manifest published as machine-readable data: artifact name, owning ticket, producing check, freshness window
security_privacy: The gate reads artifact metadata and results; it never copies customer data into an evidence bundle
A waiver is itself evidence: recorded, dated, expiring and attributable
observability: Gate result and the list of failing artifacts are published without opening the board, so beta readiness is a number rather than an opinion
tests: Full-pass test against a complete fixture set
rollout_rollback: The gate is written and run in report-only mode as its contributing artifacts appear, so its first blocking run is not its first run
Rollback is disabling the blocking behaviour, which returns the decision to a human checklist and is recorded as a deliberate downgrade
non_goals: The public-launch gate, which T-REL-03 owns
Producing any of the underlying evidence, which the contributing tickets own
Go-to-market and marketing readiness
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Owns the gate definition, the evidence manifest and the waiver rule. Every artifact it reads is produced by another ticket in that ticket's own repository.

items.title: Run the public-launch evidence gate
items.outcome: One executable gate decides whether public launch may proceed: the beta gate still green, Play approval in hand, load, soak and chaos results within budget, a penetration test with no open high or critical finding, a staffed support path, and the production evidence that only exists once real traffic does.
items.context: Private beta and public launch fail for different reasons. Beta fails on correctness and compliance; launch fails on scale, on a store decision we do not control, and on the absence of anyone to answer a user. Separating the two gates keeps the beta gate honest - it does not wait on a penetration test that cannot be scheduled yet - and keeps the launch gate from being a rubber stamp on the beta one.
scope: Re-run of the T-REL-02 beta gate as a precondition, with its freshness window applied
Play approval evidence: the permissions declaration decision and the production track availability
Load, soak and chaos results within the published budgets, dated against the release candidate
Independent penetration test with every high and critical finding closed and retested, plus the red-team outcomes
Support readiness: intake live, response targets published, an on-call rota and a named escalation path
Production evidence: a proven restore in production, an alert that reached a human, and a rehearsed production rollback
Billing readiness: purchase, renewal, refund and entitlement replay green against the production configuration
Accepted-risk register reviewed, with no expired entry
acceptance_criteria: The gate fails unless the beta gate is green and within its freshness window
The gate fails without Play approval evidence; the approval is a third-party decision and is never assumed
Load, soak and chaos results are present, dated against the release candidate, and within the published budgets
No high or critical penetration-test finding is open, and every closed one has a retest record
Support intake is live, its response targets are published, and an on-call rota with an escalation path is recorded
A production restore, a production alert that reached a human, and a production rollback rehearsal are all evidenced
Billing replay is green against the production configuration rather than a staging one
No accepted risk in the register has passed its expiry
A manual override is impossible; an exception requires a recorded, dated, expiring waiver with a named owner
contracts_schema: Extends the T-REL-02 evidence manifest with the launch-only artifacts and their freshness windows
security_privacy: Penetration-test findings are referenced by identifier in the gate, and the report itself stays in its restricted location
Production evidence records the fact and the timestamp of a drill, never a data extract
observability: Launch readiness is published as the same artifact list and pass or fail result, so the state is visible without a meeting
tests: Full-pass test against a complete fixture set
rollout_rollback: Run in report-only mode from the start of beta so the missing artifacts are visible early rather than at launch
Rollback is disabling the blocking behaviour, recorded as a deliberate downgrade with an owner
non_goals: Producing any of the underlying evidence, which the contributing tickets own
The private-beta gate, which T-REL-02 owns
Pricing, marketing and launch communications
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Owns the launch gate definition and its manifest extension. Every artifact it reads is produced elsewhere, and it creates none of them.
